info.title: Thicket
info.description: Thicket's versioned REST API. The web app runs on the same routes, so everything the product does is here. Human-readable reference: https://www.thickethq.com/developers/api

get.description: Identity, owners, plan limits, can-do flags, and settings for the caller's organization (any member). `logo` is omitted when unset.

patch.description: Owner only. A new name gives the account a new address: its slug is rebuilt as `{slugified-name}-{key}` around its permanent `key`, and the answer carries it. Every earlier address keeps resolving in the `{orgSlug}` segment (by the key, and a pre-July workspace's pre-rename slug by `legacy_slug`, which its first rename sets), and the API never redirects, so a path built from an old slug keeps working. A client holding the workspace by `id` or `key` sees no change; one holding it by slug refreshes its organization list.

name.description: Validated as POST /orgs validates a name: 1 to 100 characters with at least one letter or number in any script (422 invalid otherwise). Refused with 422 (invalid) when it carries a link: a scheme such as https://, a www. address, or a domain followed by a path. A bare domain such as Linear.app is a name and is accepted. Resending the current name is always accepted and changes nothing, even one set before these rules.

slug.description: The account's address now: rebuilt from the new name around the permanent key when the name changed it, the same slug otherwise.

409.description: The new name would give the account an address another account has (`conflict`). Choose a different name.

delete.description: Owner only, effective immediately: the org turns invisible everywhere, any Stripe subscription is cancelled, and every owner gets a confirmation email. Data is retained for a 30-day restore window (POST /api/v1/orgs/{orgId}/restore); after that the purge task hard-deletes rows and storage.

get.description: Owner only; the response is a JSON attachment. `?projects=id,id` limits content to those projects (people, companies, and groups always ride along). Private chats and personal notes are never included; use /account/export/chats for transcripts.

parameters.name: projects
parameters.description: Comma-separated project ids to limit the content

get.description: Owner only; deliberately split from the account export because of the privacy weight it carries. Transcripts (participants plus author, timestamp, and content lines) for the chosen conversations, as a JSON attachment.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated DM recording ids, at least one

get.summary: Private conversations for the private-chats export
get.description: Owner only. Every private conversation in the organization with its participants' names, line count and last activity, most recent first, for choosing which GET /account/export/chats exports.

get.summary: Projects the account export can carry
get.description: Owner only. Every active and archived project, the ones the owner isn't on too, A to Z; never a template or the list library. GET /account/export takes these ids in `projects`.

put.summary: Upload or replace the account logo
put.description: Admin and up. Multipart upload, `logo` field, any decodable image up to 5 MB; the server re-encodes it to a square webp.

delete.description: Admin and up.

get.summary: Storage usage vs the plan limit
get.description: Total usage, the plan's limit, and the largest files. Private-chat and unposted-draft uploads count toward usage but are never listed.

Everything that happened across your accessible projects, newest first, ready to group by day client-side. Page with `per_page` and follow the `Link: rel="next"` header, whose URL carries the next page's opaque `cursor` (rows written between requests neither repeat nor shift pages); `page` still answers. Same visibility rules as the Latest-activity page: trashed content and non-client-visible recordings filtered, chat and DM lines never logged. Filters: `project_id`, `person_id` (the actor), `starred=1` (your starred projects), `since` (ISO datetime), `q` (matches title, actor name, or content text).

parameters.name: person_id
parameters.description: Only this actor's events

parameters.name: starred
parameters.description: Pass 1 to limit to your starred projects

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only events at or after this instant

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Comma list of event actions, e.g. card_added,move (a container-watch poll)

parameters.name: recording_type
parameters.description: Only events about recordings of this type

parameters.name: parent_id
parameters.description: Only events about recordings inside this container (a column, a list): the container-watch poll

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Keyword filter: title, actor name, content text, or the name of someone added to a project (an `access_changed` row)

200.description: Activity events, newest first (default page size 50)

get.description: People only, in the named-agents pilot (`403 agents_unavailable` elsewhere). Owners and admins see every agent; anyone else sees only their own personal agent. Project names are filtered to the caller's access. Who may give an agent work is the connector's local setting (`thicket connect setup`).

post.description: Owners and admins only (Admin › Manage agents). Creates a shared agent: a member with no sign-in that reaches only the projects it is given. A personal agent is created by its owner on the connection approval page.

patch.description: `{name, project_ids}` renames the agent and replaces its projects: owners and admins for a shared agent, its owner for a personal one (projects the caller can see; hidden ones are kept). `{enabled: false}` deletes the agent (its owner, or an owner or admin): its connection is revoked, running work is interrupted, and its past content keeps it as the author. `{enabled: true}` answers 422: a deleted agent can't be restored.

delete.description: Its owner (personal) or an owner or admin. An agent has one connection; its tokens stop working on their next request and its listening session ends. A request already in progress may finish.

post.summary: Attach a file to rich text
post.description: Stores a file for a post's rich text: embed the returned `url` in the post's HTML (an `img` src for an image, an `audio` src for a voice note, an `a` href otherwise). Creating or saving the post that embeds it makes it that post's attachment: an `upload` recording with this same id whose parent is the post, listed in the post's `content_attachments` and by `GET /recordings/{post_id}/children?type=upload`, never in Docs & Files. It takes the post's audience, is trashed and restored with it, and stays with it if a later edit drops the embed. Until a post claims it, only its uploader can read it (`url`, `download_url`), and a file no post claims is deleted after 24 hours. Two forms. `multipart/form-data` with `file` (required, up to 50 MB) stores the bytes at once and answers the stored file. `application/json` with `filename` and `byte_size` (up to 10 GB) reserves the file and answers presigned storage URLs (`mode` `single`: PUT the whole file to `url` with the same `content_type`; `multipart`: PUT each `part_size` slice to `part_urls[n-1]` and keep each response's ETag), so the bytes go straight to storage; then call `completeAttachment`. A reservation is not ready, readable or claimable until completed; cancel it with `abandonAttachment`. Send the composer's place: `project_id` for a post in a project, or `dm_id` for a line in a direct message (a participant's, clients included); with neither (My Notes), only members of the team may attach, and both is a 422. A dm line that embeds the file claims it like any post, so deleting the line deletes it. Returns 402 when the plan's storage cap is reached. Files for Docs & Files go to `POST /recordings/{folder_id}/uploads` instead; `POST /recordings/{dm_id}/uploads` still posts a file straight into a dm (its cover image).

file.description: The file bytes, up to 50 MB, non-empty

project_id.description: The project of the post the file will be attached to

dm_id.description: The direct message whose line the file will be attached to (instead of project_id)

duration_ms.description: A recording's length in whole milliseconds (a voice note), kept with the file and served as `duration_ms` wherever the file is listed; up to a day

byte_size.description: The file's exact size in bytes, up to 10 GB; complete checks the stored object against it

content_type.description: Sent again as the PUT's Content-Type in single mode

project_id.description: The project of the post the file will be attached to

dm_id.description: The direct message whose line the file will be attached to (instead of project_id)

duration_ms.description: A recording's length in whole milliseconds (a voice note), kept with the file and served as `duration_ms` wherever the file is listed

201.description: The multipart form: the stored file, waiting for a post to claim it. The JSON form: the reservation and its presigned storage URLs

delete.description: Deletes a file from `POST /attachments` that no post has claimed yet, for a composer whose author removed it before posting, or cancels a reservation mid-transfer (its stored parts go too). Only the uploader's own; once a post has claimed the file it belongs to the post and this answers 404 (edit the post instead).

parameters.name: attachmentId
parameters.description: The id `POST /attachments` returned

post.description: After PUTting the bytes of a file reserved with `createAttachment`'s JSON form: completes the multipart upload (send every part's ETag in `parts`; a single PUT sends no body), checks the stored object is the size reserved, and makes the file ready, so the post that embeds its `url` claims it and its uploader can read it. Only the uploader's own; answering again for a ready file is harmless. A file whose stored size differs is scrapped (404): reserve it again.

parameters.name: attachmentId
parameters.description: The id `POST /attachments` returned

etag.description: The ETag header storage answered that part's PUT with

200.description: The verified file, waiting for a post to claim it

get.description: Tier, subscription status, trial and period dates, plus usage against the plan's limits. In `limits`, -1 means unlimited; one `people` pool covers members and guests alike, clients included.

post.summary: Switch plans on the live subscription
post.description: Owner only. Swaps the price on the existing Stripe subscription with prorations, never a second subscription, and syncs the local row in-request so the change reads back immediately. 404 when there is no live subscription; 422 when the account is already on that plan. A downgrade below the org's active-project count is allowed: the org lands over-limit and the home chooser archives projects down, restorably.

Owner only. Verifies the price (from GET /api/billing/prices) and returns a Checkout URL to redirect the buyer to. The signup trial is the only trial an org ever gets: a session created mid-trial carries a trial_end aligned to the existing end date, never restarted, and every other org is charged at checkout. Under 48 hours of trial left checks out as an immediate charge. An account that already holds a subscription is refused with 409 already_subscribed: plan changes go through POST /billing/change-plan, the card and invoices through POST /billing/create-portal.

400.description: Unknown, inactive, or non-Thicket price (code bad_request)

409.description: The account already has a subscription (code already_subscribed); change plans with POST /billing/change-plan

post.summary: Create a Stripe customer portal session
post.description: Owner only: payment method, invoices, and cancellation. The optional `{"flow": "subscription_cancel"}` body deep-links the portal's cancel-subscription confirmation (404 without a subscription). Plan switching is not portal work; it rides /billing/change-plan.

get.description: Published platform announcements, newest first: global content read through an org-scoped URL, personalized per viewer ({{first_name}} interpolated, excerpts capped at 200 chars).

The way to open an `action: "announced"` notification row (those carry a bulletin_id instead of a recording_id). Published bulletins read for anyone in the org; a draft reads only for someone holding their own tray row for it (a test send), everyone else gets 404. Reading marks the caller's notification row read, same as opening the page.

200.description: The announcement, personalized for the caller

get.description: Events (and optionally due tasks) across every accessible project's calendar plus the account calendar. Recurring events expand at read time: each occurrence arrives as its own row carrying `occurrence_key`, the anchor-zone day key the occurrences DELETE endpoint speaks. `from`/`to` accept ISO 8601 with an explicit offset, or a zoneless wall clock interpreted in the caller's resolved zone (their /me timezone preference, then the tz cookie, then UTC).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Window start; offset or zoneless wall clock

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Window end

parameters.name: just
parameters.description: `me`: only items you created or are invited to

parameters.name: tasks
parameters.description: Include due to-dos and cards (per-request view state, not persisted)

parameters.name: projects
parameters.description: Comma-separated project ids to limit to

parameters.name: calendars
parameters.description: Comma-separated calendar container ids (a project `calendar` tool's `container_id`, up to 50) to limit events to, so a project's extra Calendar shows only its own events. Pair it with `projects` for one project's calendar page. Dated to-dos and cards (`tasks`) are the project's and are not narrowed by it.

parameters.name: starred
parameters.description: Limit to your starred projects

post.description: Invitees (`participant_ids`) are notified. `project_id` null or omitted targets the account calendar: org-level events with no project, non-clients only. Datetimes accept an explicit offset or a zoneless wall clock resolved in the caller's zone. All-day events are floating dates, encoded T00:00:00Z to T23:59:59Z by convention.

project_id.description: null or omitted: the account calendar

calendar_id.description: Which of the project's calendars (a `calendar` tool's `container_id`) when it holds several; omitted: its first. Ignored for the account calendar; another project's calendar is 404

content_html.description: Rich notes (sanitized); wins over `content` when both are sent

link.description: A join link (video call etc.); reminders carry it

recurrence.description: The repeat schedule; null means the event does not recur (clears it on update)

participant_ids.description: Membership ids to invite; they are notified

visible_to_clients.description: A project event's "Who should see this?"; omitted means the project's `share_new_items_with_clients` default. Ignored on the account calendar

patch.description: Edits apply to the whole series for recurring events; to change one day, or one day onward, use the occurrences PATCH endpoint, and to delete them the occurrences DELETE. Invitees are notified of the change. Same fields as create, all optional. `recurrence: null` stops the event recurring. A series keeps its own `exdates` whatever the request sends: each names a day that lives on as its own event or in the trash. `project_id` (and `calendar_id`) moves the event to another calendar; a move alone writes nothing else.

project_id.description: Move the event, with its repeating pieces, onto this project's Calendar (it must be switched on), or null for the account calendar. Comments come along; invitees are not told of a move alone.

calendar_id.description: With `project_id`: which of that project's Calendars (a `calendar` tool's `container_id`); omitted, its first. 422 without `project_id`.

content_html.description: Rich notes (sanitized); wins over `content` when both are sent

recurrence.description: The repeat schedule; null means the event does not recur (clears it on update)

post.summary: Copy an event to a calendar
post.description: Copies the event onto a project's Calendar or (`project_id` null) the account calendar; a repeating event copies as one repeating event. Comments stay behind unless `include_comments` (they keep their authors and times). A client is refused (403); anything but an event, or a project without a Calendar the caller can see, is a 404.

project_id.description: The project whose Calendar receives the copy, or null for the account calendar

calendar_id.description: Which of the project's Calendars (a `calendar` tool's `container_id`); omitted, its first

get.description: "Add to my calendar": the event as a credential-authenticated iCalendar download (Content-Disposition: attachment). Recurring events export a year of occurrences. For an ongoing subscription mint a feed instead.

get.summary: Where a day of a repeating event now lives
get.description: For a link, notification or bookmark that names a day of a repeating event (`?occurrence=`) which may since have changed on its own or been deleted: the recording that holds the day now. `split: true` with the piece that took the day (its own event, `series_id` naming the series; `status: trashed` for a deleted day waiting in the trash, or a deleted "all future" part that repeats from it), else the series itself. `occurrence` is the day to open when what holds it repeats; null when the day is neither the series' own nor held by any piece (deleted for good, or never one of its days). An event that does not repeat answers itself.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The repeating event

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The day's anchor-zone key (YYYY-MM-DD), as the link carries it

delete.summary: Delete an occurrence of a recurring event
delete.description: The trash prompt for recurring events ("Only delete this event" / "Also delete all future events"); recurring events only. What's deleted goes to the trash (`trashed_id`), and restoring it (`PUT /recordings/{trashed_id}/status/active`) puts the dates back into the series. Default: just this occurrence (`result: excluded`; the day is trashed as its own event). `?mode=future`: this and every later occurrence (`result: truncated`; the series ends the day before and the rest is trashed as one repeating event); from the first occurrence that trashes the whole series (`result: trashed`, `trashed_id` is the event itself). `date` is the occurrence's `occurrence_key`, the anchor-zone day key from the calendar listing; never derive it from `start` client-side. 404 when the series has no occurrence that day.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The occurrence's anchor-zone day key (YYYY-MM-DD)

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: `future`: also delete all later occurrences

trashed_id.description: What went to the trash; restoring it undoes the deletion

patch.summary: Edit an occurrence of a recurring event
patch.description: The edit prompt for recurring events. Default ("No, just change this event"): the day splits off as its own event, linked to the series by `series_id` and `occurrence_key`, and takes the edit. `?mode=future` ("Yes, change future occurrences too"): the series ends the day before and a copy repeating from this day takes the edit; from the first occurrence the whole series is edited in place. Invitees hear about the change as with any edit, and a new date or time logs `rescheduled`. Returns the event that now carries the change, or the series unchanged when nothing changed. Same fields as editing an event, all optional. 404 when the series has no occurrence that day.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The occurrence's anchor-zone day key (YYYY-MM-DD)

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: `future`: this and every later occurrence

content_html.description: Rich notes (sanitized); wins over `content` when both are sent

recurrence.description: `?mode=future` only: how the event repeats from this day on (a single day repeats with its series). `exdates` is ignored

get.summary: The calendars you can put an event in
get.description: The account calendar first (`project_id` null; never for a client; `calendar_id` null until its first event makes it), then every switched-on Calendar of the active projects you can open, the sample project included and templates never: projects A to Z, each project's Calendars in tool order. Create into one with `POST /calendar` (`project_id`, `calendar_id`), move an event with `PATCH /calendar/{eventId}`, copy one with `POST /calendar/{eventId}/copy`.

Your active (unrevoked) feeds. Each `url` is a capability URL: the token in the path is the only credential the public /feeds/{token}.ics endpoint checks, so treat it like a password. Revoked feeds return 404 there.

post.description: A token-authenticated read-only ICS feed honoring the filters, for subscribing an external calendar app. The returned `url` is the capability: anyone holding it can read the feed until you revoke it. Clients cannot mint feeds and receive 404.

project_id.description: Legacy single-project scope; cannot be combined with project_ids

project_ids.description: Selected projects and/or the account calendar. Omit for all calendars. Cannot be combined with project_id.

starred_only.description: Follow your starred projects as they change (the calendar's Starred pick). Cannot be combined with project_id or project_ids (422).

url.description: The public /feeds/{token}.ics URL; the token is the credential

project_ids.description: Acknowledged selection, or null for all calendars

delete.description: Effective immediately: the feed's public URL starts returning 404. Only your own feeds are revocable.

get.description: Prefill for the event form: "Team call Friday at 10am" becomes a title plus a start (and end, when a range was given). A suggestion the user confirms, never a silent commit. Relative dates and clock times mean the viewer's zone. When nothing date-like is found, the datetime fields come back null.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The text to parse

get.description: Defaults are seeded per organization.

post.description: Admin and up.

patch.description: Admin and up.

delete.description: Admin and up; deleting clears the category from posts.

get.description: Your conversations, latest activity first, with participants and a preview of the last line, your unread lines and whether it is frozen. Direct chats have no project, never appear in activity, and are visible only to their participants. `?status=archived` lists archived ones: readable (and searchable) forever, but no new lines post into them.

post.description: Finds the existing conversation with exactly these people or starts one; either way the `dm` recording comes back with 201. Your own id alone starts a chat with just yourself. You can message admins, owners, and anyone you share a project with. Lines are chat children: POST /recordings/{chat_id}/children with type chat_message; archive via PUT /recordings/{id}/status/archived (for everyone, cannot be undone).

get.description: A private chat as your conversations list it, archived ones included. Anyone not in it gets a 404.

patch.summary: Name a chat or set its cover
patch.description: `title` names the conversation (up to 150 characters; empty or null names it for its people). `cover_upload_id` sets its cover to an image posted into this chat (`POST /recordings/{dmId}/uploads`), or removes it with null; anything else posted here is a 422, and an upload elsewhere a 404. An archived chat changes no more (404). A client names a group, and sets or removes its cover, only when they started it (403).

get.description: The people you may start a private chat with, A to Z: owners and admins reach everyone; anyone else the owners, the admins and whoever shares a project with them. Nobody in a company whose private chats are off is offered. While your own company's private chats are off, `restriction` names it with how many people it holds and `people` is empty.

delete.description: Only whoever left the cheer, or an org admin or owner (403 otherwise; 404 when already gone). Works for recording cheers and event cheers alike.

get.description: Companies with counts of active memberships, the account's primary company first (`is_primary`), then by name. Removed memberships are excluded.

patch.description: Rename, toggle client status, or toggle `dms_disabled` (the per-company private-chat restriction: members drop from chat pickers, can't start DMs, and existing conversations freeze read-only both ways). The account's primary company is renamed here, apart from the account's own name, and can't be made a client company (403 `primary_company`).

delete.description: People keep their membership; they just lose the company association. The account's primary company can't be deleted (403 `primary_company`).

post.summary: Turn a URL into sanctioned embed markup
post.description: Server-generated embed markup for the allowlist: YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, Spotify, X, Flickr, Imgur, SoundCloud, and direct `.gif` URLs. Non-allowlisted URLs return `{html: null}`: keep a plain link. Client-supplied iframe HTML is never accepted anywhere; the returned markup also round-trips the rich-text sanitizer.

200.description: The markup, or null for a non-allowlisted URL

get.description: Every event across the projects you can see, oldest first in strict (created_at, id) order, so a poller that keeps the `position` each page answers never misses a row and never sees one twice: pass it back as `cursor` to read on from there. `since` starts a fresh read at an instant; `project_id` narrows to one project (and is how the sample project is read). Up to 100 a page; `has_more` says whether a page is full. Rows carry `performed_by` (the actor's membership id), `actor_kind` and `authored_via` (the machine channel that wrote what the event is about, or null for a person's own work). Same visibility rules as the activity timelines: trashed content and what a client cannot see stay out, chat and direct-message lines are never logged.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Rows per page; default and at most 100

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Start a fresh read at this instant

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Only this project's events

200.description: A page of events, oldest first, and the position to resume from

position.description: Pass as `cursor` on the next read; the last row's position, or the one you passed when nothing new arrived, null on a first empty read

get.summary: List cheers on a change-log event
get.description: Cheers on one row of a recording's change log. The per-recording events listing already inlines the same shape.

post.description: Up to 16 characters of text or emoji. Notifies the event's actor through their `notify_cheers` channel, bundled into one notification per recording within 3 hours. An exact duplicate returns 200 `{already_cheered: true}` instead of 201.

200.description: Already cheered with exactly this content

get.summary: What the account-wide browsers hold for you
get.description: Whether All check-ins shows for the caller: it appears once check-in content exists for them in a project they can reach (a client's share alone).

Every message, comment, doc and file, or check-in answer across the active projects the caller can reach, newest first, 50 a page with `Link: rel="next"` carrying `?cursor=`. A client's share alone; never the sample project's. Docs and files narrow by `kind`, by `uploader_id` (repeatable), and by `attachments`, on by default: files attached to posts, and files in the caller's private chats, join the list.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Docs and files: one kind

parameters.name: uploader_id
parameters.description: Docs and files: only what these people posted

parameters.name: attachments
parameters.description: Docs and files: include files attached to posts and private chats (default true)

get.description: Account-wide home-screen groupings of projects. Move a project in or out via PATCH /projects/{id} with `folder_id` (or null).

post.description: Any non-client member can manage folders; clients get 403.

patch.summary: Rename, recolor, or reorder a folder
patch.description: Any non-client member; clients get 403.

delete.description: The folder's projects drop back to the top level. Any non-client member; clients get 403.

get.description: Groups bundle non-client people for @-mentions and pickers. Removed memberships are excluded; groups with no active members remain in the list.

200.description: The organization's groups with their members

get.description: The services a project link is added from, in the order a chooser lists them, "External Service" (`other`) last. `id` is what a project link's `service` takes; `prompt` and `placeholder` are the URL field's label and example for that service.

The account's to-do list templates by title: active ones, or `?status=archived`. Clients and outside collaborators receive an empty list. Each is a to-do list in a hidden library: open, fill and edit it through the recording routes (`GET /recordings/{id}` and its children), and archive, trash or restore it with `PUT /recordings/{id}/status/{status}`, which `can_archive` says you may do (restoring an archived one is open to everyone who sees it).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Defaults to active

post.description: A new, empty to-do list template from a name and a description, filled afterwards like any list. Clients and outside collaborators receive 403.

name.description: Refused with 422 (invalid) when it carries a link: a scheme such as https://, a www. address, or a domain followed by a path. A bare domain such as Linear.app is a name and is accepted.

post.summary: Use a to-do list template in a project
post.description: Copies the list, its groups, to-dos, notes and assignments to the end of the project's To-dos, team-only. Assignees not on the project join it when you may change its people, else their assignments are dropped; clients and removed people are dropped. An archived template, or one you can't see, answers 404.

project_id.description: The project whose To-dos receive the list

get.description: Owners and admins only; anyone else gets 403. Each merge keeps the merged-away person's address.

post.description: Irreversible dedupe: the winner inherits the loser's assignments, subscriptions, project access, and authorship.

get.description: Agent identities only. Oldest first, up to 100 requests from the last 30 days. Everything addressed to the agent lands here, from any person or agent but itself, on content it can read: `mentioned`, `assigned`, `subscribed` (a new comment or chat line where it follows), `watched` (a new to-do or card in a list or column it watches), `pinged` (a direct message), `completed` (something it follows was completed) and `cheered` (a cheer on its own post). Who may direct the agent is decided by its connector from local settings. A pending request whose source changed or that the agent can no longer read is dismissed. Terminal or running rows whose content is no longer readable carry only id, status and result.

post.summary: Claim, settle or dismiss a request
post.description: Requires the live runtime lease. `claim` moves a pending request to running (several can run at once; a second claim of one request fails). `completed`/`failed` settle work this runtime holds. `dismissed` closes a pending request the connector doesn't admit, with a short `result` (for example `not_trusted`). Posting a reply is a separate content operation, written as the agent.

post.summary: Start, renew or stop the listening lease
post.description: Agent identities only. Renew within 60 seconds; one runtime per agent (`403 agent_busy`). A runtime that takes the lease dismisses pending requests made more than a minute before it (`result: "before_this_run"`): requests made while nothing is listening are not picked up later. Stopping or losing the lease marks running requests interrupted; nothing is retried.

get.description: Open to-dos, cards and card steps assigned to you across projects, grouped into `priorities` (your Up Next list, in your order; items carry `priority_id`) and `non_priorities`. Card steps are normalized under their parent card as `children`: the card is pulled in even when only a step is assigned, and a prioritized step surfaces its card. get.description: `{unread_count, notifications}`, newest first. Event and due-date reminders sweep lazily on every read (the count-only arm included) with DB-level dedupe, so reminder rows land exactly once even under concurrent reads. Reminder rows are delivery receipts, and the tray (and `unread_count`) shows only the newest per entry: one per event occurrence (its day-before, hour-before and starting-soon) and one per dated to-do or card (its due tomorrow, due today, overdue by a day and overdue by a week, across due-date changes); cursor reads return every receipt. Rows carry `bulletin_id` for platform announcements (action `announced`, actor-less) and `bundle_count` for chat rows: lines folded into one entry while it stayed unread. Project-chat rows use action `chatted` for the push-worthy idle-edge delivery and `chat_activity` for the quiet bundled tray row, both pointing at the room recording; visiting the room marks them read. **Cursor reads:** pass `since` (the last row's `created_at`) and `after` (its id) to walk forward, oldest first; the response then carries `next_cursor` to pass next time. Rows carry the actor's membership id, role and kind. Bundled notifications are context, not executable requests. Named agents use `/my/agent/inbox` and `/my/agent/session`.

post.description: Admins and up; owner invites require an owner. `note` rides the invitation email as plain text, and a note with a link, web address or email address is refused with 422 (invalid) before anything is written or sent; `project_ids` are granted on accept. The email carries a decline link that stamps the invite declined and notifies the inviter. Plan seat limits apply. One invitation per address per workspace: inviting an address that already has a pending invitation folds into it. New `project_ids` pool onto that invitation and go out as the 'added you to' follow-up on its original join link (201); with nothing new to grant the call answers 403 (already_invited) and sends nothing, resend is the nudge. A declined or expired invitation is revived and re-sent on the same link, under the reminder cooldown (403 invitation_send_cooldown inside an hour of the last invitation email to that address). The invitation and email job are committed together; email delivery runs after commit and retries transient failures. Success confirms queuing, not provider delivery. A global email pause returns 503 (email_paused) before changing the invitation.

An outside collaborator or a client can't become an admin or owner (403): make them a member first. `role: "client"` also strips group memberships and access to projects that don't work with clients. `employee: false` makes an outside collaborator, who stops following all-access projects they aren't on. A person's company follows their type: becoming an owner, admin or member puts them in the account's primary company, and becoming an outside collaborator or a client takes them out of it, to no company. `company_id` can't move an owner, admin or member out of the primary company (403 `coworker_company`) or put anyone else in it (403 `primary_company`).

patch.description: `color` is a preset card color; anything outside the enum is a 400. `starts_on` and `ends_on` travel together: set both or null both, and `ends_on` must not precede `starts_on` (violations are a 400). `show_activity` toggles the project's activity rollups. `clients_enabled: false` reverts every recording in the project to team-only and clears the client company (Work with clients); it waits for the clients to go: while a client is on the project's roster it is a 403 `clients_on_project` and nothing changes, so remove each client first (PUT /projects/{projectId}/people with `revoke`). `client_company_name` is the label shown on the project. Move the project in or out of a home-screen folder with `folder_id` (or null). `timesheet_enabled` switches the project's Timesheet (a project-details edit: never clients, and "Restrict who can edit project details" applies); the response then carries it. `wallpaper_mode` is how the project's wallpaper paints (`fill` or `tile`); the image itself is PUT/DELETE /projects/{projectId}/wallpaper. schema.description: UTF-8 with no BOM, LF line endings and RFC 4180 quoting. Header `Date,Person,Hours,Regular,Overtime,Project,Item,Notes,Created` (then `Status` while approvals are on), then one row per counted entry, newest day first, then newest logged. No totals row. Hours is the combined total; Regular and Overtime are its two portions, all as decimal strings ("2.0", "1.5", "0.12"); Item is "{Type}: {title}" (To-do, Message, Document, File, Card or Event), empty for time on the project itself; Created is ISO 8601 with the caller's UTC offset. A Person, Project, Item or Notes value that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return gets a leading apostrophe, so spreadsheets read it as text, never as a formula. While approvals are on, a last `Status` column says where each entry's week stands: Approved, Submitted, Changed, Rejected or Not submitted.

A Person, Project, Item or Notes value that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return gets a leading apostrophe, so spreadsheets read it as text, never as a formula. schema.description: UTF-8 with no BOM, LF line endings and RFC 4180 quoting. Header `Date,Person,Hours,Regular,Overtime,Project,Item,Notes,Created` (then `Status` while approvals are on), then one row per counted entry, newest day first, then newest logged. No totals row. Hours is the combined total; Regular and Overtime are its two portions, all as decimal strings ("2.0", "1.5", "0.12"); Item is "{Type}: {title}" (To-do, Message, Document, File, Card or Event), empty for time on the project itself, and the absence type for absence (Project "Absence"); Created is ISO 8601 with the caller's UTC offset. A Person, Project, Item or Notes value that starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return gets a leading apostrophe, so spreadsheets read it as text, never as a formula. A token that does not match its kind (an APNs token is hex, on an iOS device) is a 422. Dead tokens are pruned automatically when the transport reports them (APNs 410 Unregistered or BadDeviceToken).

get.summary: Start Sign in with Apple in the app's browser tab
get.description: For a native app with no Apple SDK: the app opens this address in its browser tab (a Custom Tab), keeping the PKCE verifier its `challenge` hashes. It answers 302 to Apple with the flow's state cookie. Apple's answer signs the tab in, through the web's two-factor page when the account has two-factor on, and lands on `GET /native/apple/finish`, which sends the tab back to the app at `thicket://auth/apple` with a one-time `code` or an `error`. `terms=1` says the person accepted the Terms of Service and the Privacy Policy in force (`GET /signup-policy`), which a new account needs: without it, a new account comes back as `error=TERMS_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED`. 503 `apple_unavailable` where Apple isn't configured.

parameters.description: base64url(SHA-256(code_verifier)), PKCE's S256 transform of a verifier the app keeps

get.summary: Return from Sign in with Apple to the app
get.description: Where Apple's flow lands in the app's browser tab; not called by the app itself. Signed in, it mints a single-use `code` for that sign-in, good for two minutes and bound to the `challenge`, ends the tab's own session, and answers 302 to `thicket://auth/apple?code=…`. Refused, it answers 302 to `thicket://auth/apple?error=…` with `TERMS_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED`, `ACCOUNT_UNAVAILABLE`, `SIGNUP_UNAVAILABLE`, `AGENT_SIGN_IN_FORBIDDEN` or `account_not_linked` (each but the first with the server's `message` to show), or `failed` for anything else.

post.summary: Exchange a sign-in code for a session
post.description: The app exchanges the `code` its browser tab brought back, with the PKCE `code_verifier` whose S256 transform was the `challenge`, for a session, returned in `set-auth-token` (send it as `Authorization: Bearer`, as from Better Auth's own sign-in). Anonymous by design: the code and the verifier are the credential. Any attempt spends the code, and every refusal reads alike (401 `invalid_grant`: unknown, expired, used, or a verifier that doesn't match). An account that can't sign in answers 403 with its code (`account_unavailable`). Rate-limited per caller address.

A native app reads it before making an account and sends both back as `legalAcceptance: {accepted: true, termsVersion, privacyVersion}` (Better Auth's camelCase) on `POST /api/auth/sign-up/email`, or under `additionalData` on `POST /api/auth/sign-in/social` for a Google or Apple account that does not exist yet; an acceptance naming any other version is refused with `400 TERMS_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED` and no account.

personalAccessToken.description: Personal access token from My settings → API tokens (`thicket_pat_…`). The token acts as its user: same organizations, project access, role, and row-level security as their sign-in. `read`-scope tokens may only GET/HEAD (writes → 403 `read_only_token`). Bearer requests must send a User-Agent naming the app and a contact (URL or email) or they receive 400 `user_agent_required`. The web app's own session cookie is also accepted on every route.

sessionToken.description: A Better Auth session token presented as a bearer, the native apps' credential. Sign-in responses (`/api/auth/sign-in/email`, `/api/auth/sign-in/social`) carry it in the `set-auth-token` header; send it back exactly as issued, as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is the same session a browser holds in its cookie and is treated exactly like one: full scope, no User-Agent requirement, no token rate limit. Told apart from a personal access token by the `thicket_pat_` prefix, which session tokens never carry.

oauthBearer.description: OAuth access token bound to https://www.thickethq.com/api/v1, obtained through browser approval with PKCE. thicket.read allows GET/HEAD; thicket.write allows mutations within current user permissions. MCP-bound tokens are not accepted. User-Agent is required. Manage grants in My settings, Connected apps.

schedule.description: Check-in questions only, as on a row of `GET /recordings/{recordingId}/questions`: when it asks, as the sweep reads it. Absent for a question without a readable schedule and on every other recording

time_zone.description: Check-in questions only: the IANA time zone the schedule's `hour` and `minute` are on; null when `schedule` is absent

askees.description: Check-in questions only: who it asks

answer_count.description: Check-in questions only: its answers you can see

recent_answer_count.description: Check-in questions only: answers in the last 24 hours

next_asks_at.description: Check-in questions only: when it next asks, at its hour in `time_zone`; null without a schedule, while paused, and in a template

paused.description: Check-in questions only: it has stopped asking everyone

opted_out.description: Check-in questions only: you asked it to stop asking you

template.description: Check-in questions only: the question is in a template, which never asks and takes no answers

answerable.description: Check-in questions only: `POST /recordings/{recordingId}/answers` takes your answer, as on the questions listing's rows

last_commenter_name.description: Who wrote the latest active comment, by name; null with none

has_public_link.description: A public link is live on it (messages, documents and files; the team's Public mark). Always false for a client

assignees.description: client_approval, card, todo and step rows only

step_count.description: card rows only: active steps under the card

subtask_count.description: todo rows only: active subtasks under the to-do

completed_by_name.description: todo and card rows only: who completed it, by name; null while open

trashed_by_name.description: Who put it in the trash, by name; null outside the trash

archived_by_name.description: Who archived it, by name; null outside the archive, and null when the Admin › Archiving sweep did it

on_hold.description: card rows only: parked in its column's On Hold section

role.description: column rows only: Triage, Not Now or Done; null for a custom column

color.description: column rows only: the column's color from the to-do group palette (`PUT /recordings/{recordingId}/color`); null when none

hold_enabled.description: column rows only: whether its On Hold section is on

permissions.description: GET /recordings/{recordingId}/todo-outline, /board, /children and /message-board rows: what you may do to the row, as the write decides, read once for the page

card_count.description: column rows only: active cards in the column (held cards included)

todo_open_count.description: todolist rows only: open to-dos in the list, its groups included

todo_done_count.description: todolist rows only: completed to-dos, groups included

item_count.description: folder rows only: the active documents, files, linked files and subfolders it holds (what is shared, for a client)

byte_size.description: upload rows only: the current version's size

duration_ms.description: upload rows only: a recording's length as its uploader declared it (a voice note); null without one

content_type.description: upload rows only: the current version's MIME type

TodoOutline.description: A To-dos tool or a list in one read: the tool's lists (`lists`), a list's groups (`groups`), and the open to-dos directly inside (`todos`, the tool's loose to-dos or the list's own).

list.description: For a list: the list itself as a row, with its open and done counts (its groups included), its standing and `permissions`; absent for the To-dos tool

todos.description: Its open to-dos outside any group, in position order
Its open to-dos, in position order

Board.description: A board or one of its columns in one read: the columns in board order, each with its cards.

board_id.description: The board the columns are on (the read's own id for a board)

subscribed.description: Whether you are subscribed to the column: told of new cards and its comments

collapsed.description: Whether you collapsed it for yourself (`collapsedColumns` in `/my/ui-state`)

cards.description: Its active cards, at most 500, held ones included; Done's newest finished first, else in position order

MessageBoardSort.description: A Message Board's order, one setting for everyone on the board.

sort.description: `newest` newest post first, `activity` latest comment first, `alpha` A to Z by title

MessageBoard.description: A Message Board in its order: the pinned messages first, then the rest.

sort.description: The board's order, `newest` when it was never set

pinned.description: The pinned messages, most recently pinned first (ten at most)

messages.description: The other messages in the board's order, cut at `limit`

has_more.description: More messages follow the cut; ask again with a larger `limit`

edited_at.description: When its author last edited it; null if never

InlineCheer.description: A cheer as embedded on chat rows, comments and change-log events.

RecordingCheerRow.description: One row of the standalone cheers listing. On the sample project, the cheers its seeded people left come first: each keeps the same `id` on every read, carries the nil uuid as `membership_id`, and can't be removed.

membership_id.description: Who cheered. The nil uuid (`00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`) on a sample project cheer, which no member has.

RecordingEvent.description: One change-log row: what happened, who did it, and its cheers.

action.description: created, completed, moved, version_added, visibility/hold/comment toggles, ...

detail.description: moved rows carry fromParentTitle/toParentTitle captured at move time

RecordingReference.description: A recording whose content links to this one (the References tab).

RecordingPersonRow.description: One person on an assignee or subscriber list.

email.description: In full to owners and admins and to the person themselves; redacted for everyone else, agents included: the name's first character, then a dot for every other character of the name and every character of the domain but its periods ("j••••@•••••••••.•••").

ids.description: The affected ids; for copy, the copies' ids

group_id.description: group action only: the created group

PendingAttachment.description: A file stored for a post's rich text, waiting for the post that embeds `url` to claim it.

id.description: The attachment's id; the upload recording the post's claim creates keeps it

duration_ms.description: The length declared with it (a voice note), in milliseconds; null without one

url.description: The stable inline route to embed in the post's HTML (`/api/v1/{org}/uploads/{id}/file`)

UploadReservation.description: A file reserved in a folder with `createUpload`'s JSON form: where to PUT its bytes. Single mode PUTs the whole file to `url`; multipart mode PUTs each `part_size` slice to `part_urls[n-1]` (the last may be shorter). The URLs expire after 12 hours and the reservation after 24. Post it with `postUploads`.

url.description: Single mode: the presigned PUT URL

part_urls.description: Multipart mode: one presigned PUT URL per part, in order

part_size.description: Bytes per part (every part but the last)

AttachmentReservation.description: A file reserved with `createAttachment`'s JSON form: where to PUT its bytes. Single mode PUTs the whole file to `url`; multipart mode PUTs each `part_size` slice to `part_urls[n-1]` (the last may be shorter). The URLs expire after 12 hours and the reservation after 24.

id.description: The attachment's id: complete it, then embed `/api/v1/{org}/uploads/{id}/file`

url.description: Single mode: the presigned PUT URL

part_urls.description: Multipart mode: one presigned PUT URL per part, in order

part_size.description: Bytes per part (every part but the last)

CheckInSchedule.description: When a check-in question asks. Daily uses `days`; weekly and every_other_week use `day_of_week`; monthly means the first `day_of_week` of the month unless `day_of_month` is set. A response carries `minute` always and only the day field its frequency reads, with the defaults applied (a daily question's weekdays, Monday for a missing `day_of_week`).

days.description: Daily only: which weekdays to ask (0=Sunday to 6=Saturday; default Monday to Friday, weekends allowed)

day_of_week.description: Weekly, every_other_week, and default monthly shape; the every-other-week alternation anchors at creation

day_of_month.description: Monthly alternative to the first-weekday shape

ProgressDot.description: One tracked to-do list on the progress chart.

position.description: 0 = working it out, 1 = getting it done

color.description: Assigned at first track, stable across re-tracks

ProgressSnapshotDot.description: A dot as captured in a saved update's snapshot.

url.description: The /public/{token} capability URL: anyone holding it can read the sanitized content

created_at.description: When the live link was made; null while unpublished

created_by_name.description: Who made the live link, by name; null while unpublished, or when they have left

ProjectFolder.description: An account-wide home-screen grouping of projects.

UploadVersion.description: A kept past version of a file.

created_at.description: When this version was superseded by the next

download_url.description: Relative API path of this version's download redirect

content.description: Up to 16 characters of text or emoji

subject_type.description: What `subject_id` names: a recording, a cheer (`RecordingCheerRow.id`), or a person (a membership id)

reason.description: Harassment or bullying, Hate or discrimination, Threats or violence, Sexual content, Spam or a scam, Private information shared, Something else

person.description: Whom the report concerns while they are still in the organization, so a client can offer to block them: the person reported, or the author of what was reported; null for words no member wrote (the sample project's) and for someone since removed

person_blocked.description: Whether you already blocked that person

image.description: Same-origin avatar path or external URL; null means render an initials disc

TimesheetEntry.description: Hours on a project, on one of its items, or as absence: a team-only recording. It counts while its item exists, goes to the trash and comes back with it, and moves with it. Clients never see one, and no generic `/recordings` route returns one.

occurrence_date.description: The day of a repeating event; null otherwise

regular_hours.description: Regular portion of hours, as a decimal string. hours is regular_hours plus overtime_hours.

overtime_hours.description: Overtime portion of hours, as a decimal string. Existing entries default to "0.0".

id.description: For a `timesheet` parent, the project's timesheet: `POST /recordings/{id}/timesheet/entries` there logs time on the project itself

title.description: "Timesheet" for time on the project itself

app_url.description: The item's page (a repeating event's carries `?occurrence=`), or the project's timesheet page

TimesheetEntryParent.description: What the time is on: the item, or the project's timesheet (`type: "timesheet"`) for time on the project itself; null for absence.

TimesheetWeekRow.description: A row of the weekly timesheet. An entry is in the row whose `recording_id` and `occurrence_date` are its `parent.id` and `occurrence_date`; new time in the row goes to `POST /recordings/{recording_id}/timesheet/entries` with `occurrence` set to `occurrence_date`.

recording_id.description: What its time hangs under: the item, the recording holding a repeating event's day, or the project's timesheet (time on the project itself)

item.description: Null for time on the project itself

added.description: Added to the week (it stays without hours); false when only its hours put it there

can_log.description: New time can go in it

closed_reason.description: Why it takes no new time, when it doesn't

week_starts_on.description: The org's timesheet week start (Admin › Timesheets)

writable.description: The caller can change this week: their own, or an owner's or admin's view of someone still on the team

has_history.description: The person has ever added a row or logged time, however it was entered: the first-run hint shows while false (an empty week alone means nothing, since every week starts empty)

status.description: The week's approval status; null while approvals are off

As read now: `changed` once the week's hours no longer match what was submitted or approved (an edit, a new or deleted entry, a trashed or restored item, a move; never a notes-only edit), until it's resubmitted or approved again. A rejected week stays `rejected` until it's resubmitted

changed_since.description: A changed week: whether it changed since it was submitted or since it was approved

submitted_by.description: Who submitted it: the person, or an owner or admin for them

decided_at.description: When it was approved or rejected; null while it waits on a decision

self_approved.description: An owner or admin approved their own week

approval.description: Who submitted and decided the week, and when (the `TimesheetWeekApproval` shape); null while approvals are off

total_hours.description: The week's total, decimal hours as a string

rows.description: By project name, then time on the project, then items

archived.description: Removed: here only while it has hours this week

projects.description: What a new row can be in: active projects with their Timesheet on that the person is on. Empty when the week isn't writable

entries.description: The person's counted entries dated in the week, newest day first

completed.description: A to-do or card that's done; false for everything else

parent.description: Its parent: a to-do's list, group or to-do (a subtask), a card's column, a document's or file's folder, a message's board, an event's schedule. A tool goes by the project's name for it

occurrence.description: A repeating event's day: pass it as `occurrence` when adding the row

day.description: An event's day in the caller's zone; null for other items

TimesheetPickerContainer.description: Where the weekly timesheet's item picker files an item: a to-do's list or group (a subtask's, its to-do's), a document's or file's folder, a card's column, a message's Message Board; null for events, which go by `day`. A tool (the To-dos for loose to-dos, the top of Docs & Files, the Message Board) goes by the project's name for it

parent.description: The list a to-do group sits in, or the folder a subfolder sits in; null right under the tool

status.description: As read now: `changed` once the week's hours no longer match what was submitted or approved (an edit, a new or deleted entry, a trashed or restored item, a move; never a notes-only edit), until it's resubmitted or approved again. A rejected week stays `rejected` until it's resubmitted

changed_since.description: A changed week: whether it changed since it was submitted or since it was approved

submitted_by.description: Who submitted it: the person, or an owner or admin for them

decided_at.description: When it was approved or rejected; null while it waits on a decision

self_approved.description: An owner or admin approved their own week

hours.description: The week's counted hours in projects the caller can see (absence included), decimal hours as a string

removed.description: No longer on the team: their week still takes a decision

week_starts_on.description: The org's timesheet week start (Admin › Timesheets)

weeks.description: A row per person with time or a submission this week, by name

without_time.description: The team's current people with neither, by name

waiting.description: Submitted or changed weeks from any other period, oldest first

all_approved.description: Everyone with time this week is approved and unchanged

orgSlug.name: orgSlug
orgSlug.description: The organization's URL slug, any earlier slug of it (each carries the organization's permanent `key` as its last segment), or the bare key; list yours via GET /api/v1/authorization or /api/v1/orgs. Resolved, never redirected: a path built from a slug that has since changed keeps working.

cursor.name: cursor
cursor.description: The next page's position, opaque. Take it from a `Link: rel="next"` URL and never build one; it supersedes `page`.

Link.description: RFC 8288 `<url>; rel="next"` naming the next page, with every filter of this request kept. Absent on the last page. Follow the URL as given rather than building page URLs.

Unauthenticated.description: No valid credential (invalid, expired, or revoked tokens included)

Forbidden.description: Authenticated but not allowed (role, client visibility, read-scope write, session-only route)

NotFound.description: Missing or not yours: cross-tenant probes are indistinguishable from missing

Validation.description: The body parsed but a field is invalid

PlanLimit.description: The organization's plan cap was reached (code limit_reached)

RateLimited.description: Over a rate limit: 50 requests per 10 seconds per token, 50 per 10 seconds per client address for token traffic, or the address's session budget for the web and native apps; honor Retry-After (seconds)
